title_en: Jiejie Co., Ltd. v. Trademark Review and Adjudication Board of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce and Third Party Jinhua Baizi Cosmetics Co., Ltd. — administrative dispute over trademark opposition review
ruling_gist_en: Where a party asserts that a trademark constitutes a work protected by copyright law and claims that the disputed trademark infringes its prior copyright, a comprehensive consideration of relevant evidence is required for determination. Where the copyright registration certificate is dated later than the filing date of the disputed trademark, the fact that the trademark was created prior to the filing date may be established by reference to evidence such as the trademark registration certificate issued before the filing date, web pages containing the trademark, newspaper content, and physical products. Where a trademark registration certificate alone is insufficient to prove prior copyright, all evidence in the case may be comprehensively considered. When it is confirmed that the relevant evidence corroborates each other and forms a complete evidence chain, it may be determined that the party enjoys prior copyright in the trademark.

杰杰有限公司与国家工商行政管理总局

商标评审委员会、第三人金华市百姿化妆品

有限公司商标异议复审行政纠纷案

【裁判摘要】

当事人以商标标志构成受著作权法保护的作品，主张诉争商标损害其在先著作权的，需要综合考量相关证据予以认定。在著作权登记证明晚于诉争商标申请日时，可以结合诉争商标申请日前的商标注册证、包含商标标志的网站页面、报刊内容、产品实物等证据，确认商标标志的形成时间早于诉争商标申请日的事实。在仅凭商标注册证不足以证明在先著作权时，可以综合考量全案证据，在确认相关证据相互印证，已形成完整的证据链时，可以认定当事人对该商标标志享有在先著作权。

最高人民法院行政判决书

（2017）最高法行再35号

再审申请人（一审原告、二审上诉人）：杰杰有限公司。住所地：美利坚合众国加利福尼亚州92614欧文阿姆斯壮大街17361号。

法定代表人：艾里克·霍尔，该公司财务总监。

委托诉讼代理人：罗正红，北京罗杰律师事务所律师。

委托诉讼代理人：丛林，北京罗杰律师事务所律师。

被申请人（一审被告、二审被上诉人）：国家工商行政管理总局商标评审委员会。住所地：中华人民共和国北京市西城区茶马南街1号。

法定代表人：赵刚，该委员会主任。

委托诉讼代理人：马君丽，该委员会审查员。

一审第三人：金华市百姿化妆品有限公司。住所地：中华人民共和国浙江省金华市金东区曹宅工业区。

法定代表人：洪霞，该公司董事长。

委托诉讼代理人：雷东，北京中知律师事务所律师。

委托诉讼代理人：李建芳，北京中知律师事务所律师。

再审申请人杰杰有限公司（原名非常面孔化妆品有限公司，以下简称杰杰公司）因与被申请人国家工商行政管理总局商标评审委员会（以下简称商标评审委员会）、一审第三人金华市百姿化妆品有限公司（以下简称百姿公司）商标异议复审行政纠纷一案，不服北京市高级人民法院(2015)高行（知）终字第3565号行政判决，向本院申请再审。本院于2016年7月19日作出(2016)最高法行申2038号行政裁定，提审本案。本院依法组成合议庭，公开开庭审理了本案。再审申请人杰杰公司的委托诉讼代理人罗正红、丛林，一审第三人百姿公司的委托诉讼代理人雷东、李建芳到庭参加诉讼，被申请人商标评审委员会未到庭参加诉讼。本案现已审理终结。

杰杰公司申请再审称，（一）杰杰公司在再审中提交的8份新证据，进一步补强证明其对羡慕标志作品享有在先著作权，再结合杰杰公司在原审诉讼期间提交的证据，足以初步证明其对“”（ENVYDOTLOGO，以下简称羡慕标志）作品享有在先著作权。（二）羡慕标志作品不仅满足著作权法规定的作品属性，也满足商标法规定的商标属性。杰杰公司提交的关于在先著作权的证据足以证明，在被异议商标申请日之前，非常面孔化妆品有限公司（TOO FACED COSMETICS, INC.，以下简称非常面孔公司）已在中国大陆使用了“羡慕标志”和“ TOO FACED”两个商标，并在美国及中国具有一定影响。百姿公司以不正当手段抢注被异议商标，依法不应予以核准。（三）作为相关涉案作品和商标现在权利人的非常面孔化妆品有限责任公司（TOO FACED COSMETICS, LLC），与本案处理结果存在利害关系，应当追加其参加本案再审诉讼。综上，二审判决认定事实和适用法律错误，请求本院撤销二审判决及商评字（2013）第19020号《关于第5165219号“TOOFACED及图”商标异议复审裁定书》（以下简称被诉裁定），判令商标评审委员会对杰杰公司针对第5165219号“TOOFACED及图”商标提出的异议复审请求重新作出复审裁定。

商标评审委员会提交书面意见辩称，被诉裁定认定事实清楚，适用法律正确，作出程序合法，杰杰公司的再审申请理由不能成立，请求本院予以驳回。

百姿公司述称,（一）杰杰公司提交的新证据在被异议商标申请日之前形成，不属于《中华人民共和国行政诉讼法》（以下简称行政诉讼法）规定的新证据，不应予以采信。（二）杰杰公司提交的证据自相矛盾，不能证明其对羡慕标志作品享有在先著作权。（三）杰杰公司没有提交任何在相关产品上使用羡慕标志的证据，不能证明其在中国大陆地区在先使用“羡慕标志”及“TOO FACED”商标并具有一定影响。杰杰公司也没有证据证明百姿公司在被异议商标申请日之前已经接触到羡慕标志，其关于百姿公司以不正当手段抢注其在先使用并具有一定影响商标的主张，不能成立。（四）商标保护具有地域性，杰杰公司在其他国家或地区获得商标注册证的事实，并不能受到我国商标法的保护。综上，请求本院依法驳回杰杰公司的再审申请。

杰杰公司向北京市第一中级人民法院（以下简称一审法院）起诉请求：撤销被诉裁定，判令商标评审委员会重新作出复审裁定。

一审法院认定事实：被异议商标为第5165219号“TOOFACED及图”商标，由百姿公司于2006年2月20日申请注册，指定使用在第3类化妆品、清洁制剂、指甲油、香皂、香水成套化妆用具等商品上。

在被异议商标初审公告期限内，杰杰公司提出注册异议。国家工商行政管理总局商标局（以下简称商标局）作出（2011）商标异字第26280号“TOOFACED及图”商标异议裁定书，裁定杰杰公司所提异议理由不成立，被异议商标在指定商品上的注册申请予以核准。杰杰公司不服该裁定，于法定期限内向商标评审委员会申请复审，请求依据2001年修正的《中华人民共和国商标法》（以下简称商标法）第十三条、第三十一条、第十条第一款第（八）项以及第四十一条规定，不予核准被异议商标注册。杰杰公司向商标评审委员会提交了商标异议复审申请书及相关材料等证据。

2013年6月24日，商标评审委员会经审查作出被诉裁定。该裁定认定：1. 结合杰杰公司提交的证据，证据1为杰杰公司在美国的商标注册证明；证据2为杰杰公司自行制作的图片且无法确定形成时间；证据3、4为外文证据，杰杰公司仅就少部分予以翻译，且均为杰杰公司自行制作并无其他证据佐证；证据5为杰杰公司罗列的商标注册信息。上述证据无法证明杰杰公司对被异议商标中所涉的图形享有在先著作权，故被异议商标的申请注册未构成商标法第三十一条所指损害他人现有在先权利之情形。2. 杰杰公司提交的证据不足以证明在被异议商标申请注册之前，杰杰公司在与被异议商标指定使用的化妆品、香水等商品为同一种或类似商品上，已经将与被异议商标相同或近似的标识作为商标使用并使之具有一定影响，故杰杰公司援引商标法第三十一条“不得以不正当手段抢先注册他人已经使用并有一定影响的商标”的规定，请求不予核准被异议商标的注册的主张缺乏依据。3. 结合杰杰公司提交的在案证据，尚不足以证明在被异议商标申请注册前，杰杰公司已将“TOOFACED”系列商标在中国市场在第3类化妆品等商品上进行使用，亦不足以证明“TOOFACED”商标在中国已成为相关公众广为知晓并享有较高声誉的驰名商标，故被异议商标的注册未构成商标法第十三条第一款所指的不予注册并禁止使用的情形。同时，鉴于杰杰公司在被异议商标申请注册前，未申请注册有“TOOFACED”商标，故本案不适用商标法第十三条第二款对已注册驰名商标保护的规定。4. 杰杰公司还主张被异议商标的注册违反了商标法第十条第一款第（八）项之规定，但该项规定的情形涉及的是公序良俗或公共利益，此条款适用的前提是该商标的使用造成了对公共利益的损害。杰杰公司所称被异议商标的注册使用对其权益的损害不属于该条款调整范畴，且被异议商标本身未构成对社会公共利益产生消极负面影响，故被异议商标不属于商标法第十条第一款第（八）项所指之情形。杰杰公司主张被异议商标违反了商标法第四十一条第一款“以欺骗手段或其他不正当手段取得注册的”情形亦缺乏事实依据。综上，商标评审委员会依据商标法第三十三条、第三十四条规定，裁定：被异议商标予以核准注册。

一审诉讼中，杰杰公司提交了中华人民共和国国家版权局的作品登记证书、美利坚合众国版权局登记证明、作品存档证明、著作权转让证明、美国商标注册证明、百度搜索材料等证据材料，以证明如下内容：美术作品羡慕标志（ENVYDOTLOGO）存档于美国版权局，著作权登记号为VA1-902-220，作品完成年份为1997年，首次发表日期为1998年11月9日，首次发表国为美国，作者为杰杰公司，通过2014年4月的书面转让协议转让给非常面孔化妆品有限责任公司，转让生效日为2011年12月22日。该作品于2014年4月18日在美国版权局进行登记，2014年8月28日在中华人民共和国国家版权局进行登记。羡慕标志作为商标于2005年11月29日在美国专利商标局注册，商标权人为非常面孔化妆品有限责任公司，有效期为10年；TOOFACED作为商标在2012年3月27日在美国专利商标局注册，商标权人为非常面孔化妆品有限责任公司，有效期为10年。

此外，杰杰公司明确其本案诉讼的实体法律依据为商标法第三十一条，其权利为在先著作权。杰杰公司另确认美术作品羡慕标志、羡慕标志商标和TOOFACED商标的权利人均为其关联公司非常面孔化妆品有限责任公司。

一审法院认为，本案应适用2001年商标法进行审理。关于被异议商标的注册是否违反了商标法第三十一条的规定。被异议商标于2006年2月20日申请注册，其商标主要图形与羡慕标志（ENVYDOTLOGO)图形较为相似。但就杰杰公司主张的在先著作权而言，虽然杰杰公司提供了作品登记证书、登记证明、作品存档证明、著作权转让证明等证据，但上述证据形成的日期均在2014年，在被异议商标申请注册日期之后，而美国商标注册证明等证据仅能证明商标注册的相关情况，对于著作权而言证明力不足。故杰杰公司提供的证据不足以证明在被异议商标申请日之前，其在中国大陆地区对羡慕标志享有著作权。商标评审委员会据此认定被异议商标未构成对杰杰公司在先著作权的侵犯，并无不当。杰杰公司主张百姿公司是出于主观恶意，违反诚实信用原则，以不正当手段抢注杰杰公司在先使用并有一定影响商标，但杰杰公司就此并未提交其在先使用及具有影响力的有效证据，该项主张不能成立。

一审法院于2015年6月18日作出（2014）一中知行初字第1430号行政判决：驳回杰杰公司的诉讼请求。案件受理费100元，由杰杰公司负担。

杰杰公司不服一审判决，向北京市高级人民法院（以下简称二审法院）上诉请求：撤销一审判决和被诉裁定，判决商标评审委员会重新作出复审裁定。

二审法院认定事实：二审期间，杰杰公司补充提交了杰罗德·布兰丁出具的《作品申明》，称杰杰公司主张著作权的羡慕标志作品系其于1997年创作完成。百姿公司对该证据不予认可。因杰罗德·布兰丁出具的《作品申明》仅相当于证人证言，鉴于杰罗德·布兰丁并未出庭作证、该证据系二审诉讼新提交的证据及行政诉讼的合法性审查原则等因素，二审法院对该证据不予采信。

二审法院认为，本案主要是审查被异议商标于2006年2月20日申请注册时是否损害了杰杰公司在异议复审程序中所主张的在先著作权，而根据杰杰公司的主张，在被异议商标申请注册时是杰杰公司而不是非常面孔化妆品有限责任公司系杰杰公司所主张的在先著作权的权利人，且杰杰公司针对被异议商标提出了注册异议，并于2011年9月12日提出了异议复审，故杰杰公司应当向商标局或者商标评审委员会提供其享有在先著作权的证据。同时，杰杰公司所主张的在先著作权系其转让给非常面孔化妆品有限责任公司，作为转让人的杰杰公司主张转让前的商标注册侵犯其在先著作权，其通常比作为受让人的非常面孔化妆品有限责任公司更便于提供被异议商标是否损害其著作权的相关证据。因此，杰杰公司是本案的适格主体，其作为原告提起本案诉讼有利于查明被异议商标是否损害其在先著作权的事实，一审法院未通知非常面孔化妆品有限责任公司作为本案当事人参加一审诉讼，尚不致对杰杰公司主张的在先著作权造成实质性损害，故不宜通知非常面孔化妆品有限责任公司作为第三人参加二审诉讼。

杰杰公司主张被异议商标的注册损害其在先著作权，其应举证证明在被异议商标的申请日之前其在中国大陆地区形成了合法的在先著作权。杰杰公司虽然提供了作品登记证书、登记证明、作品存档证明、著作权转让证明等证据，但上述证据形成的日期均在2014年，即均在被异议商标申请注册日期之后，而美国商标注册证明等证据仅能证明商标注册的相关情况，并不能证明杰杰公司享有在被异议商标申请注册时即对羡慕标志图形享有著作权。因此，一审法院认定杰杰公司提供的证据不足以证明在被异议商标申请日之前，其在中国大陆地区对羡慕标志作品享有著作权并无不当，商标评审委员会据此认定被异议商标未构成对杰杰公司在先著作权的侵犯亦属正确。在此基础上，由于杰杰公司主张其于2011年12月22日将羡慕标志图形的著作权转让给非常面孔化妆品有限责任公司，但鉴于杰杰公司在本案中无法证明其于被异议商标注册申请时对羡慕标志作品享有著作权，故杰杰公司有关被异议商标损害了非常面孔化妆品有限责任公司在先著作权的上诉理由不能成立。此外，杰杰公司虽主张被异议商标构成以不正当手段抢注其在先使用并有一定影响商标，但杰杰公司并未提交其在中国大陆地区在先使用被异议商标并具有影响力的有效证据，故一审法院对杰杰公司该主张不予支持亦无不当。

二审法院于2015年12月2日作出（2015）高行（知）终字第3565号行政判决：驳回上诉，维持一审判决。一、二审案件受理费各100元，均由杰杰公司负担。

在本院再审审查及审理程序中，杰杰公司向本院提交了以下三组证据：

Group 1: Evidence to prove that JieJie Company owns prior copyright in the Envy Logo Work. Including: 1. Registration No. VA 851-298, Certificate of Copyright Registration of the United States. It is intended to prove that on December 22, 1997, Jerrod Blandino, founder and director of JieJie Company, registered the predecessor "ENVY" series works of the Envy Logo Work for copyright in the United States, with both the copyright owner and author being Jerrod Blandino. This series of works is the predecessor of the Envy Logo Work. 2. The May 1998 issue of VOGUE magazine. It is intended to prove that the predecessor "ENVY" work of the Envy Logo Work was publicly published through VOGUE magazine no later than May 1998. 3. Notarial Certificate (2016) Jing Hai Cheng Nei Min Zheng Zi No. 02295, which downloaded pages of the JieJie Company website at specific past times. It is intended to prove that the JieJie Company website (toofaced.com) has continuously used the Envy Logo Work since no later than 2001. Meanwhile, at the bottom of the webpage, it is clearly stated that the copyright owner is JieJie Company, all rights reserved, i.e., "2005 Too Faced Cosmetics, Inc. All Rights Reserved." 4. The December 6, 2004 issue of the American newspaper Orange County Business Journal and the corresponding collection literature obtained from the National Library of China. It is intended to prove that the Envy Logo Work was again published in the American Orange County Business Journal. An interview report with Jerrod Blandino in that newspaper mentioned Jerrod Blandino's creative process for the Envy Logo Work, including the design of an exaggerated curvy female silhouette (i.e., "an exaggerated curvy female silhouette known as Envy"). The newspaper also published photos of TOO FACED brand cosmetics bearing the Envy Logo Work. 5. Physical products and photos of some products launched by JieJie Company in 2005. It is intended to prove that the Envy Logo Work is printed on the packaging boxes of several cosmetics launched by JieJie Company, and on the back of the packaging box it is marked "Created Exclusively by Jerrod Blandino for Too Faced Cosmetics, Inc., 2005 Copyright Owner JieJie Company, All Rights Reserved," i.e., "Created Exclusively by Jerrod Blandino for Too Faced Cosmetics, Inc., 2005 Too Faced Cosmetics, Inc. All Rights Reserved." 6. The September 2005 issue of COSMO GIRL magazine. It is intended to prove that the TOO FACED brand cosmetics of JieJie Company reported in the September 2005 issue of COSMO GIRL magazine display the Envy Logo Work, and the Envy Logo Work was again publicly published through this magazine. 7. The January 2006 issue of ALLURE magazine. It is intended to prove that the TOO FACED brand cosmetics of JieJie Company reported in the January 2006 issue of ALLURE magazine display the Envy Logo Work, and the Envy Logo Work was again publicly published through this magazine. 8. The January 2006 issue of ELLE magazine. It is intended to prove that the TOO FACED brand cosmetics of JieJie Company reported in the January 2006 issue of ELLE magazine display the Envy Logo Work, and the Envy Logo Work was again publicly published through this magazine.

Group 2: The corrected U.S. Trademark Registration Certificate No. 3020605 and the corrected work statement of Jerrod Blandino are supplementary evidence to the evidence during review and original trial. It is intended to prove that after careful recollection, Jerrod Blandino confirmed that he created the Envy Logo Work in 1997 and assigned the copyright of the Envy Logo Work to JieJie Company in 1999. The Envy Logo Work was first published on JieJie Company product packaging on November 9, 1998. The first use date and commercial use date of the Envy Logo trademark are both November 1, 1998.

Group 3: Evidence including photos of the "Kissing Booth Gloss Set" cosmetics released by JieJie Company in 2005, Notarial Certificate (2016) Jing Hai Cheng Nei Min Zheng Zi No. 03484, and Notarial Certificates (2016) Jing Hai Cheng Nei Min Zheng Zi No. 03479-03482, among others. It is intended to prove that Baizi Company had the malicious intent to preemptively register JieJie Company's prior trademark rights.

The Trademark Review and Adjudication Board, in its cross-examination, argued that except for not recognizing the authenticity of the content of Notarial Certificate (2016) Jing Hai Cheng Nei Min Zheng Zi No. 02295 in Group 1 evidence, it recognized the authenticity of the other evidence in Group 1 but believed that it could not achieve its purpose of proof. Baizi Company, in its cross-examination, argued that it did not recognize the authenticity, legality, or relevance of the Group 1 evidence, and did not recognize the probative content of the Group 2 and Group 3 evidence. This court, in its cross-examination, held that the VOGUE, COSMO GIRL, ALLURE, and ELLE magazines involved in Items 2, 6, 7, and 8 of Group 1 evidence submitted by JieJie Company were all created abroad and were not notarized and authenticated in accordance with the law; therefore, this court does not admit them. The other evidence submitted by JieJie Company is supplementary evidence to the evidence from the original trial. Because the parties have no objection to its authenticity, or although there is an objection, no contrary evidence has been submitted, this court admits this evidence and will review it in conjunction with the disputed issues.

This court holds in the retrial that the disputed issues in this case are: (1) Whether the evidence submitted by JieJie Company constitutes new evidence as provided for in the Administrative Procedure Law; (2) Whether the newly submitted evidence by JieJie Company can serve as the basis for deciding the case; (3) Whether the opposed trademark infringes upon JieJie Company's prior copyright; (4) Whether Baizi Company constitutes the act of preemptively registering another person's trademark that has been used and has a certain influence by unfair means; (5) Whether Very Face Cosmetics Co., Ltd. should participate in this lawsuit.

(1) Whether the evidence submitted by JieJie Company constitutes new evidence as provided for in the Administrative Procedure Law

Article 52 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning Evidence in Administrative Litigation stipulates that "new evidence" in Articles 50 and 51 of these Provisions refers to the following evidence: (1) Evidence that should have been permitted to be submitted with an extension during the first instance trial but was not permitted; (2) Evidence that the party applied for collection during the first instance trial in accordance with the law but was not permitted or obtained, and which the people's court collected during the second instance trial; (3) Evidence provided by the plaintiff or a third party that was discovered after the expiration of the evidence submission period.

The Administrative Procedure Law does not have specific provisions on how to deal with evidence newly submitted by a party during the retrial period. However, by reference to the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, except for evidence submitted late by a party due to intentional action or gross negligence, which the people's court shall not admit, the people's court shall admit all important evidence related to the basic facts of the case, so as to avoid deviation in the basic facts determined.

In this case, the public publication and use of the Envy Logo Work occurred not only abroad but also a long time ago, making it objectively difficult for the party to collect evidence. Furthermore, there is no evidence in this case to prove that JieJie Company intentionally delayed in submitting evidence. On the contrary, to prove its claims, JieJie Company continuously submitted relevant evidence for supplementation during the review, original trial, and retrial stages. Therefore, this court admits the new evidence submitted by JieJie Company after the second instance trial.

(2) Whether the newly submitted evidence by JieJie Company can serve as the basis for deciding the case

Among the newly submitted evidence by JieJie Company, Notarial Certificate (2016) Jing Hai Cheng Nei Min Zheng Zi No. 02295 was formed by querying previous pages of the JieJie Company website through specific means domestically. Although the Trademark Review and Adjudication Board and Baizi Company have objections to the authenticity of the content of this website, they have not submitted contrary evidence to support their claims; therefore, this court does not admit the relevant objections. The American Orange County Business Journal is a publicly distributed newspaper. Given that JieJie Company has submitted copies of the corresponding collection literature from the National Library of China, the authenticity, legality, and relevance to this case of this evidence are also not inconsistent with relevant legal provisions. The physical products and photos of some products launched by JieJie Company in 2005 indicate that the place of manufacture is China. In the absence of contrary evidence, it should be determined that these products, as evidence, were formed domestically. The corrected work statement of Jerrod Blandino, combined with the content of the interview report with Jerrod Blandino in the American Orange County Business Journal, can confirm the authenticity of its content.

(3) Whether the opposed trademark infringes upon JieJie Company's prior copyright

Paragraphs 1 and 2 of Article 19 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Administrative Cases Involving Trademark Granting and Confirmation Rights stipulate that where a party claims that the disputed trademark damages its prior copyright, the people's court shall, in accordance with the Copyright Law and other relevant provisions, examine whether the claimed object constitutes a work, whether the party is the copyright owner or other interested party entitled to claim copyright, and whether the disputed trademark constitutes an infringement of copyright. If a trademark sign constitutes a work protected by the Copyright Law, the design drafts, originals, contracts for obtaining rights, copyright registration certificates before the application date of the disputed trademark, etc., provided by the party can all serve as preliminary evidence to prove the ownership of the copyright.

Item (2) of Article 10 of the Copyright Law of the People's Republic of China stipulates that the right of authorship means the right to claim authorship and to have the author's name mentioned in connection with the work. Paragraph 4 of Article 11 stipulates that, in the absence of proof to the contrary, the citizen, legal person, or other organization whose name is mentioned in connection with the work shall be the author. The above provisions indicate that the current law adopts a presumption method for determining the identity of the author of a work. Generally speaking, the person whose name is mentioned on the work is the author. Except for special circumstances such as works made for hire or commissioned works, the author is the copyright owner upon completion of the work and has the right to transfer or license the rights legally enjoyed to others. In some special circumstances, the way the author exercises the right of authorship is not to directly sign the work but to use other appropriate means to indicate his or her authorship. Where others raise objections to his or her authorship, they shall provide contrary evidence in accordance with the law. Where there is only an objection without contrary evidence, the objection shall not be admitted according to law.

In this case, the parties do not dispute the originality of the Envy Logo Work. Baizi Company believes that the evidence of prior copyright submitted by JieJie Company cannot prove that it existed before the application date of the opposed trademark. Therefore, the following will focus on the above issue.

Although the copyright registration certificate, registration proof, work archive proof, copyright transfer certificate, and other evidence submitted by JieJie Company during the first instance trial were all formed in 2014, JieJie Company submitted Group 1 evidence to this court, the Certificate of Copyright Registration of the United States with Registration No. VA 851-298, proving that Jerrod Blandino registered the ENVY work, the predecessor of the Envy Logo Work, with the U.S. Copyright Office in 1997. The relevant content of the JieJie Company website (toofaced.com) stated in Notarial Certificate (2016) Jing Hai Cheng Nei Min Zheng Zi No. 02295 indicates that the company has used the Envy Logo Work in question since no later than 2001. The interview report with Jerrod Blandino in the December 6, 2004 issue of the American Orange County Business Journal not only mentioned Jerrod Blandino's creative process for the Envy Logo Work, including the design of an exaggerated curvy female silhouette, but also published photos of TOO FACED brand cosmetics bearing the Envy Logo Work. The physical products of some products launched by JieJie Company in 2005 indicate that the Envy Logo Work is used on the packaging boxes of several of its cosmetics. In addition to making copyright reservation statements on the company's website and relevant product packaging, JieJie Company also specifically indicated that the relevant works were created exclusively by Jerrod Blandino for JieJie Company. Although the aforementioned copyright reservation statements are generally directed at webpages or product packaging, the Envy Logo Work, as an important part thereof, should be included in the content of the aforementioned statements. U.S. Trademark Registration Certificate No. 3020605 can also clearly indicate that the trademark pattern in question containing the Envy Logo was formed no later than November 2005.

With respect to the Group 2 evidence submitted by JieJie Company during the retrial of this court, the corrected U.S. Trademark Registration Certificate No. 3020605 and the corrected work statement of Jerrod Blandino. Compared with the evidence submitted to the original trial court before correction, these two pieces of evidence clarify the first use date and commercial use date of the Envy Logo trademark as 1998, whereas the first use date and commercial use date of the Envy Logo trademark before correction were 1995 and 1996, respectively. Regarding these two supplementary pieces of evidence, JieJie Company claims that, based on the principle of good faith, after repeated verification of the creation time of the work and the first use time of the trademark, it requested the author to confirm and applied to the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office for correction. Baizi Company argued in its cross-examination that these two pieces of evidence cannot serve as supplements to the original trial evidence, that the time node, as an important reference for prior copyright, cannot be arbitrarily changed or corrected, and that the correction instead further proves the instability of the time of the Envy Logo Work and trademark. Regarding these two pieces of evidence, this court holds that whether it is the first use date of the Envy Logo trademark or the date of commercial use, both are based on the trademark owner's own statements. Although there may be instances of uncertainty regarding relevant time nodes due to the correction, in the absence of contrary evidence to overturn them and without infringing upon the lawful rights and interests of others, changes to the relevant time nodes in these two pieces of evidence will not affect the determination of the prior copyright existing before the application date of the opposed trademark in this case.

In summary, in the absence of contrary evidence, the aforementioned evidence, combined with the Certificate of Copyright Registration of the United States with Registration No. VA1-902-220, the registration proof, the work archive proof, and the copyright transfer certificate submitted by JieJie Company during the original trial, can prove that Jerrod Blandino is the author of the Envy Logo Work, and can also prove that the fact that he transferred the relevant copyright legally enjoyed to JieJie Company for commercial use after completing the creation of the Envy Logo Work occurred before the application for registration of the opposed trademark on February 20, 2006. Therefore, JieJie Company's claim that the application for registration of the opposed trademark damaged its prior copyright has factual and legal basis, and this court supports it. The determination by the court of second instance that JieJie Company did not enjoy prior copyright in the Envy Logo Work before the application date of the opposed trademark was erroneous, and this court corrects it.

(4) Whether Baizi Company constitutes the act of preemptively registering another person's trademark that has been used and has a certain influence by unfair means

Although the evidence submitted by JieJie Company regarding prior copyright can, to a certain extent, prove the fact that it used the "Envy Logo" and "TOO FACED" as trademarks priorly. However, the evidence it submitted is insufficient to prove that the aforementioned trademarks had a certain influence in China before the application date of the opposed trademark. Under these circumstances, this court will no longer examine JieJie Company's claim regarding Baizi Company's malicious intent to preemptively register JieJie Company's prior trademark. The Group 3 evidence submitted by JieJie Company to this court to prove Baizi Company's malicious intent to preemptively register JieJie Company's prior trademark is also not authenticated by this court. Therefore, this court does not support JieJie Company's claim that Baizi Company preemptively registered another person's trademark that had been used and had a certain influence by unfair means. The relevant determination by the court of second instance is correct, and this court upholds it.

(5) Whether Very Face Cosmetics Co., Ltd. should participate in this lawsuit

This case concerns JieJie Company's claim, based on its prior copyright existing before the application date of the opposed trademark, that the opposed trademark damages its prior rights and should not be approved for registration. Therefore, the substantive dispute in this case exists between JieJie Company and Baizi Company. Although during the period when the Trademark Review and Adjudication Board was hearing this case, JieJie Company transferred the copyright and other intellectual property rights of the Envy Logo Work claimed in this case to Very Face Cosmetics Co., Ltd., the disputes involved in this case were all formed before Very Face Cosmetics Co., Ltd. acquired the relevant rights. The fact that it acquired the relevant rights has no direct impact on the trial of this case. The court of second instance's decision not to support JieJie Company's application to add Very Face Cosmetics Co., Ltd. as a party does not violate legal provisions. JieJie Company's relevant claims have no factual and legal basis, and this court does not support them.

In summary, the determination in the second instance judgment that the application for registration of the opposed trademark did not damage JieJie Company's prior copyright was erroneous, and this court corrects it. The relevant grounds for JieJie Company's application for retrial are established, and this court supports them. Pursuant to Article 31 of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China as amended in 2001, Item (2) of Paragraph 1 of Article 89 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Paragraph 1 of Article 76 and Article 78 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. The administrative judgment of the Beijing High People's Court (2015) Gao Xing (Zhi) Zhong Zi No. 3565 is vacated;

2. The administrative judgment of the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court (2014) Yi Zhong Zhi Xing Chu Zi No. 1430 is vacated;

3. The Review Decision on the Opposition against Trademark No. 5165219 "TOOFACED and Device" (Shang Ping Zi [2013] No. 19020) made by the Trademark Review and Adjudication Board of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce is vacated;

4. The Trademark Review and Adjudication Board of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce shall make a new review decision on the request for review of the opposition filed by JieJie Co., Ltd. against Trademark No. 5165219 "TOOFACED and Device."

The case acceptance fee for the first instance trial is RMB 100, and the case acceptance fee for the second instance trial is RMB 100, totaling RMB 200, to be borne by the Trademark Review and Adjudication Board of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce.

This judgment is final.
